- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If model shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising forecasts) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, cap forecast growth to avoid overshoot.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overcorrects downward; if sentiment shifts to bearish post-spike, reduce forecast decline by 5–10% to allow for mean reversion.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model forecasts are rising, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid false optimism.
- If model forecast mean is significantly above true outcome mean over 30d, apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for next 7d horizon.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment swing midpoint (e.g., if sentiment shifts from 0.67 to 0.00, forecast should drop 3–5%).
- For 30d horizon, if model forecast is >10% above true outcome mean, apply downward correction based on sentiment decay rate (e.g., 1% per 3d if sentiment drops below 0.50).
